counterfactual_missing_items: No verbatim raw statement of autosomal recessive inheritance or compound heterozygosity; only '2 heterozygous mutations' is present
No raw mention of a TGM5 mutation to support acral peeling skin syndrome
No explicit raw label 'type B'; truncal involvement argues against an exclusively acral pattern
decisive_items: Revealed 2 heterozygous mutations in exon 2 of the CDSN gene
Complete separation of the stratum corneum
Clean split just above the stratum granulosum
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete candidate because the same CDSN biallelic-mutation span supports both the specific genetic etiology and the autosomal-recessive inference, while the supragranular split supports the peeling phenotype. R4 shares the CDSN etiology but omits inheritance; R3 shares the CDSN mutation but omits the gene and inheritance in its label; R2 is generic; R5 is contradicted by truncal distribution and lacks CDSN support.

rejected.why: Generic peeling skin syndrome label does not capture the specific CDSN mutation and is therefore less diagnostically complete.
Names a subtype but omits the decisive CDSN genetic etiology and the autosomal-recessive inheritance supported by biallelic mutations.
Acral subtype is not supported by CDSN mutation and conflicts with truncal involvement and the generalized biopsy findings.
